title: Keep each feature at 8 components or fewer; split it otherwise

facts.note: Planner task text mentions authoring or extending a feature and its components.
Needs an observer that counts components declared per feature in the plan artifacts (the validator test_component_count_limit already does this count).
Count-limit validator finding; available only once the validator result is surfaced to the planner.

fires: Planner writes a feature plan that lists 9 or more components
Planner adds a component to a feature that already has 8 components
doesNotFire: Feature with exactly 8 components (e.g. 2 frontend + 3 backend + 3 shared)
Editing component internals without changing the number of components in a feature

given: A planner is defining or extending a feature and its list of components.
when: The feature's component count would reach more than 8.
then: Keep the feature at ≤ 8 components; if more components are needed, split the feature into smaller features instead of exceeding 8.
prefer: Use the typical 8-component budget as a guide: about 2 frontend (presentation + application), 3 backend (application + domain + integration) and 3 shared cross-cutting components.
When a 9th component is needed, split the feature along a cohesive boundary into separate features, each within the limit.
avoid: Planning a feature with more than 8 components (e.g. 12) and letting it sprawl instead of splitting.
Gaming the count by merging unrelated responsibilities into one component or hiding components outside the feature just to stay at 8.
why: A hard ceiling of 8 components keeps features cohesive and bounded, mirroring the WMBT acceptance limits; more than 8 signals the feature is too large and should be split.
evidence: Count the components declared for each feature in the plan; every feature has ≤ 8.
Validator test_component_count_limit::test_component_count_limit passes for the planned features.
Any feature that needed more than 8 components appears as multiple split features.
verifier_detail: Threshold max_per_feature = 8 (inclusive: 8 passes, 9+ is a finding).
Typical distribution (guidance, not enforced): frontend 2, backend 3, shared 3; frontend = presentation + application; backend = application + domain + integration; shared = cross-cutting concerns.
Layers per side: frontend components live in presentation/application; backend components live in application/domain/integration.
Disposition advisory, severity 2: report findings, do not hard-fail.
